Bug_Title: TQ: Value without a type qualifier used where a value is required to have that qualifier (TQ_UNKNOWN_VALUE_USED_WHERE_ALWAYS_STRICTLY_REQUIRED)
Bug_Details:
A value is being used in a way that requires the value to be annotated with a type qualifier.
The type qualifier is strict, so the tool rejects any values that do not have
the appropriate annotation.
     
    To coerce a value to have a strict annotation, define an identity function where the return value is annotated
with the strict annotation.
This is the only way to turn a non-annotated value into a value with a strict type qualifier annotation.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where the return type is not annotated with @Nonnull, even though the method signature suggests it should be. This violates the requirement that a value is used in a way that requires the value to be annotated with a type qualifier.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases call the showBug method with a null value and an empty string. Since the showBug method does not annotate its return value with @Nonnull, using these inputs triggers the bug by violating the requirement that a value is used in a way that requires the value to be annotated with a type qualifier.
